title: Graph in the Vault: Protecting Edge GNN Inference with Trusted Execution Environment
problem: GNN model intellectual property and private graph data are vulnerable during edge deployment; existing defenses do not adequately protect both model parameters and graph topology against extraction and privacy attacks.
motivation: Edge deployment of GNNs requires protecting both model IP and sensitive graph structure from state-of-the-art link stealing attacks while maintaining practical inference performance.
method: GNNVault partitions GNNs into a public backbone model and a private GNN rectifier component, both protected within Intel SGX trusted execution environment compartments, securing both model parameters and graph data during inference without requiring full model deployment in TEE.
key_novelty: Partition-before-training design with private GNN rectifier enabling TEE-protected GNN inference with manageable TEE memory footprint.
contributions: First secure GNN deployment strategy leveraging Trusted Execution Environments
Partition-before-training methodology enabling efficient TEE utilization
Protection against state-of-the-art link stealing attacks with <2% accuracy degradation
Practical implementation with Intel SGX demonstrating feasibility
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation limited to Intel SGX without exploring other TEE platforms.
